memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, 'In the evening you will know
that it was the LORD who brought you out of Egypt, and in the morning you will
see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who
are we, that you should grumble against us?'" - Ex 16:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses says something the people have not realised: "he has heard your grumbling
against him."

They thought they were complaining about Moses and Aaron. Moses tells them the
truth. "Who are we?" Their real quarrel was never with the leadership. It was
with God, who had arranged their circumstances.

That is a searching thought. Much of our complaining is aimed at people, at a
manager, a spouse, a government, a pastor. But underneath, quite often, we are
disputing with the God who allowed our situation to be what it is.

This does not mean every complaint is sinful, or that leaders should never be
questioned. Scripture is full of honest appeals to God and frank challenges to
leaders. But it does mean we should trace our discontent back to its root and
speak to the right person about it.

Notice the promise attached: "in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD."
God's response to grumbling here is to reveal Himself. He does not merely settle
the food question. He shows them who He is.

Sometimes what we most need is not the thing we are demanding, but a clearer
sight of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose fault do you tend to think your circumstances are?
2. Is there a complaint you need to take directly to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, show me when my complaints against people are really complaints against
You. Give me an honest heart and a clearer sight of Your glory. Amen.
